source.title: Bonsai trees in your head: how the Pavlovian system sculpts goal-directed choices by pruning decision trees

confidence_rationale: Canonical, well-specified modelling of exactly the construct MECH-080 needs to exist -- a truncation set-point on forward search that varies between individuals and covaries with psychopathology. Downweighted because the truncation here is VALUE-CONTINGENT branch termination (stop on encountering a large loss), not the uniform depth cap that REE's rollout_horizon implements, and the psychopathology axis is sub-clinical mood rather than any of MECH-080's three named disorders.
failure_signatures: Pruning persisted even where it was demonstrably counterproductive, i.e. the truncation set-point did not adapt to task statistics -- a REE rollout_horizon that self-tunes to the environment would NOT reproduce this signature.

The pruning parameter is elicited by a specific event (a large loss) rather than being a standing horizon setting, so a manipulation that shortens rollout_horizon uniformly is not the same intervention as the one this paper models.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Humans planning over sequential decision trees curtail further evaluation of a branch as soon as they encounter a large loss; this pruning is reflexive and Pavlovian rather than deliberative, persists when counterproductive, and its strength covaries with sub-clinical mood disturbance.
mapping.ree_translation: Establishes the substrate premise MECH-080 rests on: forward-search depth is not fixed by the architecture but is set by a separable, individually-varying parameter, and variation in that parameter tracks affective psychopathology. In REE terms this is the closest published analog of config.e2.rollout_horizon being an individual-difference dimension rather than a hyperparameter.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Pruning is not rollout_horizon. Huys' subjects truncate CONDITIONALLY on encountering an aversive outcome; REE's rollout_horizon is an unconditional depth cap applied to every rollout. The paper therefore supports 'search depth is a psychiatrically meaningful individual difference' but does NOT license reading rollout_horizon as the parameter those individual differences load on. It also says nothing about ADHD, anxiety or OCD specifically.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adult humans, laboratory sequential-decision task with monetary outcomes; model-comparison over lookahead strategies; mood measured by self-report in the sub-clinical range.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (PLoS CB, heavily cited, explicit model comparison). Mapping fidelity is the binding constraint: value-contingent pruning vs uniform horizon cap. Transfer risk moderate -- healthy sub-clinical sample used to ground a claim about three diagnosed disorders.
